The quotation is about public investment in mainstream schools to accommodate children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) — specifically capital spending on physical adaptations (classrooms, corridors) and workforce training (teachers, teaching assistants). The core economic content is education spending and provision for a specific needs population.

Primary: **I** (Health, Education, and Welfare — specifically education infrastructure and special needs education provision)

Secondary: **J** (Labor and Demographic Economics — teacher/teaching assistant training is a substantive workforce/human capital dimension)
